stages.name: Effects of unemployment on government
stages.title: Effects of unemployment on government
stages.sub: How rising unemployment squeezes the government's budget from both sides.

steps.q: A factory closes and 200 workers lose their jobs. They used to pay income tax each month. Do they still pay it?
steps.wrong: Yes, they carry on paying it
steps.hint: Income tax is taken from wages. If there is no wage, is there tax to take?

steps.q: Those 200 workers are willing and able to work but can't find a job. Can they claim unemployment benefits?
steps.right: Yes, they become eligible for benefits
steps.wrong: No, benefits are only for those in work
steps.hint: Think about who benefits are designed to support.

steps.q: If thousands of workers across the country stop paying income tax at the same time, what happens to the total amount of tax the government collects?
steps.hint: Each worker's lost tax adds up across the whole economy.

steps.q: The government is now collecting less tax and paying out more in benefits at the same time. What does this do to its overall budget position?
steps.right: It gets worse, needing more borrowing or spending cuts elsewhere
steps.wrong: It stays balanced, since the two changes cancel out
steps.hint: Less coming in and more going out at the same time: does that improve or worsen the budget?
